category_title: Improving ELL student motivated by practical and interest-based literacy
minimal_context: Jesus is reading his choice book, Monster, during sustained silent reading time in English class.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for sustained silent reading. Please take out your choice book, Monster, and read quietly.

STUDENT: Okay. I picked this one because the story seemed realistic. I used to read pretty slow and not understand the words but now I’m a lot better.

TUTOR: That is good to hear. Please begin reading.

STUDENT: I'm trying, but the words are hard to understand in this part.

TUTOR: Just keep trying your best to read it.

STUDENT: (Puts the book down and turns to watch the other students in the class) I can't focus when these words are so hard. It just makes reading unappealing, and I'd rather see what they are doing.

options.A: Use desk carrels to provide personal space and distinguish individual reading from group activities.
options.B: Buy a classroom set of e-readers to study their usefulness during sustained silent reading.
options.C: Implement relational teaching by caring about the student and knowing his personal interests.
options.D: Incorporate frequent opportunities for the student to respond during English class reading instruction.
